# Candidate Nomination Forms for 2026 Elections available

**Published: 12th March 2026**

The Jersey Electoral Authority (JEA) has today announced the release of the official [nomination form](https://www.vote.je/nomination-process/) for individuals wishing to stand as candidates in the 2026 Elections to the States Assembly, which will take place on Sunday 7 June 2026.

**Important Information for Prospective Candidates**

Anyone wishing to become a candidate in the 2026 elections must complete the nomination form and find the support of 10 individuals willing to endorse their candidacy – one proposer and nine seconders. Prospective candidates are advised to check that their proposer and seconders are on the electoral register and eligible to vote for them.

- The form is available to download from Vote.je or a printed copy can be collected from the States Greffe, Morier House, St Helier.
- Prospective candidates can submit **one form only** and cannot stand for multiple roles on 7 June.
- Nomination forms must be completed in full and exactly as instructed on the form. Incomplete or incorrect forms will **not** be accepted.
- Forms must be delivered in person to the JEA at Morier House, Halkett Place, St Helier, JE1 1DD, between 9am-5pm on Monday 20 April, Tuesday 21 April or Wednesday 22 April 2026. Forms will not be accepted after 5pm on Wednesday 22 April 2026.
- Before submitting the nomination form, prospective candidates must send their manifesto of up to 450 words and a photograph (JPEG format, size 1-3MB) for publication on **Vote.je** and in the candidate booklet. Email submissions to: [**contact@vote.je**](mailto:contact@vote.je)

The JEA will notify the prospective candidate once their nomination form has been accepted and all accepted candidates will be publicly announced on Monday 27 April 2026.

Michael Marett-Crosby, Chair of the Jersey Electoral Authority, said: “Standing for election to the States Assembly is one of the most meaningful ways to contribute to the future of our Island. With the publication of the new nomination form, the moment arrives when candidates can prepare to stand.

“Our Island democracy is at its strongest when it reflects the diversity, experience and commitment of the people it serves. The Jersey Electoral Authority encourages all those who are passionate about Jersey, and who want to make a difference, to come forward and stand for election.”
